Figure 8 illustrates the forest plot for the sensitivity of the Bio-Rad Monolisa HCV Ag-Ab ULTRA assay in diagnosing active hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection, compared to nucleic acid testing (NAT) as the reference standard. This analysis includes all samples, regardless of their HCV antibody status. Key terms: HCV (hepatitis C virus), Ag (antigen), Ab (antibody), NAT (nucleic acid testing), TP (true positive), FP (false positive), FN (false negative), TN (true negative). 3. Figure 9 presents forest plots for the sensitivity and specificity of the Hunan Jynda HCV Core Ag ELISA assay in diagnosing active HCV infection, compared to NAT as the reference standard. This analysis also includes all samples, regardless of HCV antibody status. Key terms: HCV (hepatitis C virus), ELISA (enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay), Ag (antigen), NAT (nucleic acid testing), Ab (antibody), TP (true positive), FP (false positive), FN (false negative), TN (true negative), CI (confidence interval). 4. Figure 10 shows a bivariate analysis of the sensitivity and specificity of the Hunan Jynda Bioengineering Group HCV Core Ag ELISA assay for diagnosing active HCV infection, compared to the gold standard NAT. The plot includes pooled summary estimates (red squares), with the dashed red line representing the 95% confidence region and the dashed green line representing the 95% prediction region. Each individual circle represents a study, and the size of the circle corresponds to the total sample size. 5.
